paper_title: Mechanistic studies on Cu(NO3)2/TEMPO-catalyzed aerobic oxidation of alcohols to carboxylic acids†

questions.question: In the manuscript the authors repeatedly refer to the catalyst 'A' used in control experiments (e.g., Fig. 2A). What does 'A' refer to?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Complex A is the CuBr2–TEMPO adduct (the CuBr2/TEMPO complex characterized by X‑ray diffraction).

questions.question: What is the chemical identity (as given in the paper) of substrate 1a?
questions.ground_truth_answer: 1a is n‑C15H31CH2OH (the primary alcohol used; i.e., 1‑hexadecanol as written in the paper).

questions.question: Under the 'standard conditions' for the aerobic oxidation of alcohol 1a (Table 1 / experimental), what solvent and atmosphere were used?
questions.ground_truth_answer: Solvent: DCE (1,2‑dichloroethane); Atmosphere: O2 (O2 balloon); reaction performed at room temperature (rt) for 36 h (as the standard conditions).

questions.question: Which gave the higher yield of carboxylic acid 2a in the experiments shown in Fig. 2 (eqns (4)–(5)): using the filtrate (Cu(NO3)2–TEMPO, used as catalyst) or using the precipitate (AgBr) as the catalyst?
questions.ground_truth_answer: The filtrate (Cu(NO3)2–TEMPO) gave the higher yield: 96% NMR (isolated) yield of 2a, whereas the precipitate (AgBr) resulted in no reaction (100% recovery of alcohol 1a, i.e., no formation of 2a).

questions.question: In the control experiment carried out in the absence of KHSO4 (entry 4, Table 1 and corresponding text), what NMR yield of aldehyde 2a' was reported?
questions.ground_truth_answer: In the absence of KHSO4 (entry 4) the NMR yield of aldehyde 2a' was 61% (with 21% recovery of 1a).
